# Getting Started

Welcome to the BYU AI Foundry. You are joining a delivery team with a paying client. This
guide gets you productive in the first two weeks.

## Before the Project Starts

- [ ] Sign the client NDA or the Foundry standard mutual NDA
- [ ] Accept your GitHub invitation to the `ai-foundry-byu` organization
- [ ] Confirm your team, your role, and your QC lead
- [ ] Set up access to the project repository and approved tools
- [ ] Complete the AI Foundry baseline survey, the six Builder axes
- [ ] Read the client's proposal and any background material provided
- [ ] Review the [Build Standards](04-build-standards.qmd) and the [Program Overview](../index.qmd)

## First Two Weeks

- [ ] Attend the kick-off with the client and confirm the point of contact
- [ ] Write a one-page restatement of the problem in your own words and send it to the client
- [ ] Agree with the client on what "done" looks like and how success will be measured
- [ ] Establish the standing weekly client call and the internal team cadence
- [ ] Inventory the data you have, the data you need, and the data you are not going to get
- [ ] Identify the three assumptions that, if wrong, break the whole project

::: {.callout-tip}
The most common failure in a Foundry project is building a correct answer to a question the
client did not need answered. Spend the first two weeks making sure the question is right.
Clients expect you to question the brief in that time.
:::

## Team Roles

Every team has the same three roles. They rotate by milestone unless the team agrees otherwise.

| Role | Owns |
|------|------|
| **Client lead** | The relationship. Runs the weekly call, sends the update, owns scope conversations. |
| **Builders** | The work. Analysis, modeling, code, documents. |
| **QC lead** | The standard. Nothing goes to the client without QC sign-off. |

The QC lead's sign-off is required. Client-facing work that contains an unreconciled number or
an unexplainable model output is a QC failure, and it is graded as one.

## Where You Start on a Team

Roles say what you do. Tier says how much of it you own. Your starting tier comes from what you
have already built and shipped. Your baseline survey ratings do not set it.

| Tier | What it means |
|------|---------------|
| **Shadow** | You are on the project, in the meetings, reading the repo. You do not own a workstream yet |
| **Contribute** | You own a piece of the work, with an experienced teammate checking your work |
| **Own** | You own a workstream end to end, and the client sees your name on it |

Client lead is an Own-tier role. Students at Shadow or Contribute do not run the client
relationship in their first engagement.

Tiers move during the semester, and they are meant to. Ask your QC lead what would have to be
true for you to move up, then go do that. Nobody stays at Shadow because of a survey answer.

Teams are staffed so that every Builder axis is covered: someone on the team is strong on each
axis, though no one is strong on all six. If you are the only person on
your team strong on an axis, you were staffed for that axis.

## Your Sprints

Every student runs the same two-week [sprints](11-sprints.qmd), staffed or not. Your engagement's
own dates (kick-off, phase reviews, roll-off) are set with the client and do not change the
sprint calendar.

| Sprint | Starts | Plan due | Wrap-up due |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fri, Oct 23 | Mon, Oct 26, 11:59 PM | Fri, Nov 6, 8:00 AM |
| 2 | Fri, Nov 6 | Mon, Nov 9, 11:59 PM | Fri, Nov 20, 8:00 AM |
| 3 | Fri, Nov 20 | Mon, Nov 23, 11:59 PM | Fri, Dec 4, 8:00 AM |

### Set up your Foundry repo

We do this together in studio on October 23.

1. Create your repo from the [builder template](https://github.com/byu-strategy/builder-template),
   named `<your NetID>_foundry`, private, under your own GitHub account.
2. Add Professor Murff (`sdmurff`) as a collaborator.
3. Open the repo in VS Code, start Claude Code, and run `/sprint-plan`. The first time, it asks
   which course the repo is for: answer AI Foundry.
4. Commit and push your Sprint 1 plan, and paste its GitHub link into **Sprint 1 Plan** on Canvas.

If you also take MSB 341, keep the two repos separate.

## Your Responsibilities

- **Confirm expectations** and ask clarifying questions rather than guessing
- **Deliver on schedule.** Tell the client about a likely slip as soon as you see it
- **Come prepared** to client calls with an agenda, progress, and specific asks
- **Raise blockers within 48 hours.** Not at the weekly call, and not at the end of the sprint
- **Protect client data** per the confidentiality terms in the [Syllabus](01-syllabus.qmd)
- **Run every sprint:** plan by Monday, review and Loom demo by the Friday it ends. This is
  individual and separate from the team's client update
- **Carry your share.** Your teammates grade you on this

## What You'll Be Working On

Foundry teams ship software. Depending on the engagement, that includes:

- **Full-stack applications.** Net-new web and mobile products, B2C, B2B, or internal tools,
  built end to end and deployed to production
- **AI integration and orchestration.** Agents and copilots over the client's own data,
  automations across Slack, Notion, and their existing stack, document processing, extraction,
  routing, and summarization
- **AI enablement.** Setting the client's own team up on current agent tools such as
  Claude Code, working alongside their staff, then handing off

Discovery work comes first: where AI helps this business, what is worth building, what is worth
automating. The purpose of discovery is to decide what to build.
The engagement ends with software the client is running.
